name: run_shell
description: Execute a bash command and return stdout, stderr, and exit code. Use for running tests, git operations, pre-commit hooks, import checks, and any other shell-based verification. The command runs in the vllm-omni workspace. Avoid destructive commands (rm -rf, force push, etc).

workdir.description: Optional working directory (defaults to vllm-omni repo).

name: read_file
description: Read the contents of a file at the given path. Returns the file content with line numbers. Use this to understand existing code before editing.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to read.

offset.description: Optional line number to start reading from.

limit.description: Optional maximum number of lines to read.

name: write_file
description: Write or overwrite a file with the given content. Use this for creating new files or fully rewriting existing ones.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to write.

content.description: The full content to write to the file.

name: edit_file
description: Perform an exact string replacement in a file. The old_string must match exactly one occurrence in the file. Use replace_all=true to replace all occurrences.

file_path.description: Absolute path to the file to edit.

replace_all.description: If true, replace all occurrences of old_string.

name: grep
description: Search for a pattern in files. Returns matching files and line content. Use this to find where symbols, functions, or patterns are defined.

pattern.description: The regex pattern to search for.

path.description: Directory or file path to search (default: vllm-omni).

name: run_pytest
description: Run pytest on specified test paths. Returns the test output and exit code. Use this to verify that code changes pass the relevant tests. Always run the module's import smoke test first, then its pytest suite.

test_paths.description: Space-separated test file paths or directories (e.g. 'tests/model_executor/').

markers.description: Optional pytest -m marker filter (e.g. 'core_model and cuda').

name: run_import_check
description: Run a Python import check to verify that module imports work correctly. Use this after making code changes to verify imports are not broken.

import_code.description: Python import statement(s) to execute (e.g. 'from vllm_omni.model_executor.models.registry import *; print("OK")').

name: git_show_test_baseline
description: Show the origin/main version of a test file. Use this FIRST when a test fails — compare origin/main's test with omni's test before changing any product code.

test_path.description: Path to the test file (e.g. tests/diffusion/test_bagel.py).

name: reproduce
description: Hermetically reproduce a failing test on a CLEAN GPU. This is the ONLY sanctioned way to run a GPU test — it kills leaked stage/API processes, clears dead device locks, asserts free VRAM, and runs with CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 so a device-side assert points at the true kernel. Prefer this over raw run_shell pytest, which corrupts shared GPU state and produces phantom failures. Returns a structured outcome including whether the failure looks environmental (env_dirty) vs a real code bug.

name: run_precommit
description: Run pre-commit hooks on changed files. Use this as a final verification step after making code changes to ensure code style compliance.

files.description: Optional space-separated file paths to check (defaults to all changed files).

name: git_show_upstream
description: Show the content of a file from the upstream vLLM repo at a specific ref. Use this to see the current upstream API/signature for a file when reconciling omni changes with upstream changes.

file_path.description: Relative path to the file in the vLLM repo.

ref.description: Git ref or commit hash (default: HEAD).

name: git_show_omni_main
description: Show the content of a file from the vllm-omni main branch (origin/main). Use this to understand the original omni intent before the rebase, so you can preserve omni-specific logic while updating for upstream changes.

file_path.description: Relative path to the file in vllm-omni (e.g. 'vllm_omni/worker/gpu_ar_model_runner.py').

name: git_log_upstream
description: Show recent commit log for a file or directory in the upstream vLLM repo. Use this to understand what changed upstream since the last rebase.

path.description: File or directory path in vLLM repo.

max_count.description: Maximum number of commits to show (default: 10).

name: git_diff
description: Show the git diff of current changes in vllm-omni. Use this to review what changes have been made so far.

path.description: Optional specific file or directory path.

name: git_diff_tests_upstream
description: Show how origin/main changed test files: additions, deletions, renames, modifications. Use to understand test reorganization.

name: request_plan_review
description: Submit your plan for L4 review BEFORE making any code edits. You MUST call this after writing plan JSON + MD files and before editing any code. Pass the exact paths you just wrote to — the reviewer only reads those files, so there is no ambiguity. The L4 reviewer is a fresh, independent session — it has no access to your conversation history. It will critique your plan and return a verdict (lgtm/revise/block). The review is advisory — you retain final authority but MUST write a decision file per critique before editing code.

plan_json_path.description: Absolute path to your plan JSON file (e.g. ${LOG_DIR}/plans/${SESSION}/dispatch_initial/plan-v0-abcd.json). This is the EXACT file you just wrote with write_file.

plan_md_path.description: Absolute path to your plan markdown file. Defaults to the .md sibling of plan_json_path.

kind.description: Plan kind: 'rebase' (Phase 2 module work), 'debug' (fixing a failing test), 'repair' (fixing harness).

reviewer_model.description: Model to use for the L4 reviewer. Defaults to the orchestrator's AGENT_MODEL_L4 setting (e.g. 'claude-haiku-4-5', 'gpt-5.1', 'claude-sonnet-4-6'). Prefix determines the API: 'claude-' or 'anthropic.' routes to Anthropic; 'gpt-' or 'openai.' routes to OpenAI.

reviewer_provider.description: API provider: anthropic (Claude), openai (GPT direct), cursor (GPT via Cursor subscription). Auto-detected from model prefix if omitted.

name: search_debug_memory
description: Search past debug memory for similar failures and their proven fixes. Use this FIRST when you encounter an error — someone may have already fixed it in a previous run. Returns matching entries with symptom, root cause, and the exact fix applied.

keyword.description: Free-text search: error message, symbol name, or failure description.

module.description: Optional: filter by module name (worker_runner, model_executor, ...).

tags.description: Optional: comma-separated tags to filter by.

name: record_debug_memory
description: Record a debug memory entry after fixing a failure. This helps future runs find the same fix via search_debug_memory. Include the symptom, root cause, and the exact fix applied. Use after a successful fix.

symptom.description: What went wrong — error message, traceback summary

root_cause.description: Why it went wrong — upstream change, missing API, etc.

fix.description: How you fixed it — what code was changed and why

files.description: Comma-separated file paths that were modified

watch_outs.description: Things to watch for — similar issues in other places

name: skill_manage
description: Create or update a reusable SKILL — a distilled runbook for a recurring rebase/debug pattern. Use this AFTER you confirm a fix that is likely to recur (e.g. an upstream API drift you had to port). Skills are injected into future runs' prompts for the matching module. Prefer editing an existing skill (action=update) over creating near-duplicates.

action.description: create a new skill or update an existing one by name.

description.description: One-line summary of what this skill is for.

trigger.description: When this skill applies — the symptom/condition to match.

modules.description: Comma-separated modules this skill applies to (empty = all).

body.description: Markdown body: '## Diagnose' steps and '## Fix' template/code.

status.description: Optional: set 'retired' to deactivate a stale skill.

name: search_skills
description: List learned skills relevant to a module (and optionally matching a keyword). Skills for your module are already injected into this prompt; use this to look wider or confirm a skill exists before creating one.
